sealing.confirmation_order: For each family sort variants by tuple (hex HMAC-SHA256(nonce, canonical_json(["assignment", protocol_id, namespace, family, variant_id])), variant_id). Use ascending byte-order hexadecimal and UTF-8 variant ID as the deterministic tie break. Slots for the family consume the resulting order.
sealing.ablation_order: Use that exact family ranking formula with the independently committed ablation nonce and namespace, with two variants per family.
sealing.robustness_pairing: A reference and perturbed level share the comparison key R1–R4 as their seed key, one contrast block rather than two independent draws.
sealing.seed_derivation: For channel label in {"portable","fixed"} compute HMAC-SHA256(nonce, canonical_json(["seed", protocol_id, namespace, seed_key, channel_label])). Use int.from_bytes(first 16 digest bytes,"big"). seed_key is world ID for confirmation/ablation and the shared R1-R4 block key for robustness. canonical_json is ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), allow_nan=False, UTF-8 with no terminal newline.
sealing.commitment: SHA-256 of each raw 32-byte nonce. Keep nonce outside the repository in a phase-specific restricted work area. Published commitment is procedural separation; do not claim secrecy from someone with host filesystem access.
sealing.release: Confirmatory input-only preparation in32 requires accepted30 and31 with unchanged locked protocol, one commitment and a unique destination; actual execution in33 also requires accepted32 and exact execution/input hashes. Ablation/robustness input preparation requires accepted34; execution additionally requires their accepted input/source audit. No selector or plant call during preparation.
sealing.source_lock: The commitment receipt binds SHA-256 of raw protocol/blueprint/development recipe bytes and a Git revision containing those bytes; sealed execution source and frozen per-arm input hashes are additionally required by ticket32. Verify every path against recorded Git blobs before release.
